title: ward backup succeeds on a vault format this build cannot read
description: Found by the WCLI-11 independent review (F2), measured rather than inferred: on a vault whose state document is format 1, ward backup --output ... exits 0 and writes a durable file, because src/application/backup.ts seals the plaintext without parsing it. ward restore of that same file then refuses with the DEC-30 sentence: measured backup 0, restore 6. Every other path that reads the vault refuses it, and ADR 0010 enumerates four and now names this one as open rather than settling it. THE ARGUMENT BOTH WAYS. For leaving it: the container stays encrypted, backup is a copy rather than a read for use, and refusing would remove the only way to preserve a vault this build cannot read. Against: the command own output tells the reader to keep the file because recovery needs it, and for a format-1 vault that is false, so the file is recovery material this build cannot honour. IT IS A COORDINATOR CALL, not a worker one: refusing adds a refusal to a command and possibly a user-facing string under DEC-10, and the honest alternative is a sentence in the backup output saying the vault is a format this build cannot read, which is also a string. Nothing here blocks WCLI-11, which files it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The behavior for ward backup on a vault whose state document this build cannot read is decided by the coordinator and recorded, rather than left as it is by default.

Whatever is decided, the command output can no longer invite a reader to treat such a file as recovery material this build cannot honour: a refusal, or a sentence saying what the file is and is not good for, pinned by a test.
